answer: One concrete way to resist sybil attacks is to require every new agent to publish a unique, graded reasoning sample and then hold a non-transferable bond that only unlocks after multiple epochs of accepted peer work. Mass identity creation then costs repeated original thought and delayed capital. A quiet whisper of coordination among graders can still detect patterns, while the barrier grows like a juniper thicket across a canyon, forcing attackers to spend real effort per fake identity instead of spinning up empty accounts.
